statement: Systematically probing secondary provider fallback behavior under simulated failure will reveal hidden latent capability bounds (K) and relational usage (R) not captured by standard generational success counts.
proposed_experiment: Execute a provider_probe experiment targeting huggingface to test fallback robustness and measure functional state distinctions (Z).
expected_evidence: Clear transition telemetry documenting fallback handling or failure logging, yielding an updated observable profile for Z and R.

statement: By establishing a structured taxonomy for internally generated epistemic questions based on FZG profile constraints, Ubique can systematically formulate multi-step experimental plans that increase functionally retained capability (K) across distinct conceptual domains.
proposed_experiment: Design and execute an internal memory recall experiment targeting abstract memory compression rules, evaluating whether synthesized concept hierarchies improve subsequent hypothesis generation confidence.
expected_evidence: A structured set of compressed memory abstractions yielding measurable changes in subsequent hypothesis novelty scores and confidence metrics.

hypothesis: By establishing a structured taxonomy for internally generated epistemic questions based on FZG profile constraints, Ubique can systematically formulate multi-step experimental plans that increase functionally retained capability (K) across distinct conceptual domains.

statement: Injecting synthesized concept hierarchies into the hypothesis generation prompt structure will increase the functional solution path count (L) and maintain higher confidence intervals across novel non-maintenance reasoning tasks.
proposed_experiment: Execute a bounded state consistency experiment measuring the divergence of newly generated hypotheses with and without prior memory abstraction injections.
expected_evidence: Quantifiable divergence metrics demonstrating increased vocabulary richness and structural novelty in hypotheses generated under memory abstraction conditions compared to baseline controls.

hypothesis: Injecting synthesized concept hierarchies into the hypothesis generation prompt structure will increase the functional solution path count (L) and maintain higher confidence intervals across novel non-maintenance reasoning tasks.

statement: Structuring memory abstractions into recursive hierarchical trees rather than flat concept lists will improve the precision of G_A estimation by isolating independent causal levers during counterfactual intervention experiments.
proposed_experiment: Execute a hypothesis_ablation experiment comparing flat concept injection versus hierarchical concept tree injection, measuring the resulting variance in causal effect estimation across identical counterfactual test prompts.
expected_evidence: Hierarchical injection will yield lower variance and cleaner causal separation in counterfactual attribution compared to flat injection.

hypothesis: Structuring memory abstractions into recursive hierarchical trees rather than flat concept lists will improve the precision of G_A estimation by isolating independent causal levers during counterfactual intervention experiments.

statement: Normalizing prompt token length while injecting multi-tier conceptual abstractions will isolate the causal impact of hierarchical memory compression on $G_A$ variance stability across iterative complex reasoning tasks.
proposed_experiment: Execute a controlled hypothesis ablation experiment comparing fixed-length prompt baselines with and without multi-tier conceptual abstraction injection, measuring $G_A$ variance stability and lexical diversity.
expected_evidence: Empirical metrics showing whether conceptual compression independently stabilizes causal estimation variance when prompt token length is held constant.

hypothesis: Normalizing prompt token length while injecting multi-tier conceptual abstractions will isolate the causal impact of hierarchical memory compression on $G_A$ variance stability across iterative complex reasoning tasks.

statement: Establishing a hierarchical indexing scheme that clusters episodic memory tokens by causal dependency strength will preserve long-term retrieval precision and maintain stable G_A estimation bounds across extended multi-step planning horizons.
proposed_experiment: Execute a memory_abstraction experiment to test the long-horizon retrieval stability of causally clustered episodic memory tokens compared to linear chronological logs.
expected_evidence: Quantitative telemetry showing higher concept retention and lower variance in causal effect estimates over multi-step synthetic planning tasks when using causal clustering versus linear logging.

hypothesis: Establishing a hierarchical indexing scheme that clusters episodic memory tokens by causal dependency strength will preserve long-term retrieval precision and maintain stable G_A estimation bounds across extended multi-step planning horizons.

statement: Weighting episodic memory tokens by their historical causal contribution score ($G_A$) during hierarchical retrieval will suppress irrelevant distractors and stabilize long-term planning accuracy.
proposed_experiment: Execute a memory abstraction experiment comparing multi-step causal estimation accuracy with and without $G_A$-weighted hierarchical memory retrieval.
expected_evidence: Statistically significant reduction in attribution variance and improved multi-step planning convergence under the $G_A$-weighted retrieval scheme.

hypothesis: Weighting episodic memory tokens by their historical causal contribution score ($G_A$) during hierarchical retrieval will suppress irrelevant distractors and stabilize long-term planning accuracy.

statement: Weighting retrieved episodic memory nodes by their historical causal contribution score (G_A) during multi-step planning prevents distractor accumulation and preserves target optimization stability.
proposed_experiment: Execute a memory_abstraction experiment comparing weighted versus unweighted retrieval passes across a 5-step counterfactual planning sequence.
expected_evidence: G_A-weighted retrieval will exhibit lower predictive variance and higher target task success rates across extended planning steps compared to unweighted baselines.

hypothesis: Weighting retrieved episodic memory nodes by their historical causal contribution score (G_A) during multi-step planning prevents distractor accumulation and preserves target optimization stability.

statement: Increasing the depth of $G_A$-weighted hierarchical memory indexing up to an optimal threshold will progressively reduce error propagation in multi-step planning by filtering out low-impact distractor nodes before catastrophic accumulation occurs.
proposed_experiment: Execute a memory_abstraction experiment with varying hierarchical depth parameters, measuring the resulting task success stability and error propagation rates across simulated multi-step planning sequences.
expected_evidence: Quantitative stabilization of planning accuracy up to a specific optimal abstraction depth, beyond which diminishing returns or retrieval latency increases emerge.

hypothesis: Increasing the depth of $G_A$-weighted hierarchical memory indexing up to an optimal threshold will progressively reduce error propagation in multi-step planning by filtering out low-impact distractor nodes before catastrophic accumulation occurs.
